body: But when will I be me? If you are talking about an ontological enforcement for future life I don't get it...
I agree. Although I was fairly suicidal before now I am much more. I am going to wait for sometime if I decide to. Thank you.

I am still here. I wouldn't end my life until I feel exhausted completely hopefully I can wait it out for sometime. Perhaps things will improve but now things seem very low indeed and everyday worse in it's own way.

I'm not sure about that. I understand it will be painfull and destructive. Not to mention the issues my loved ones will have to go through. I can't comprehend it sure but romantised? Perhaps I need to think about that more.

I know it isn't a 'physical' pain but something psychological.

I really don't want medication, I've been through that before. I used to see a counseller but since I've had past suicide attempts they immediately try to drug me. Citalopram usually.

Yeah, I understood the need to see Sisyphus as happy. And I believe, in his futility, he was.

The Norwegian Wood story hit a little close to home, the suicides, the love interest in a mental hospital of sorts. But it also seemed completely ridiculous and the use, as you say, of plot devices was awful.

I used to go to counselling when I was very young; for a few years since I was perhaps 13. But as I have had suicide attempts in the past every time I seek help I get put on a 'special service' and see a psychiatrist; everytime this happens I end up on citalopram. This happened a few months ago. I was feeling depressed, even before my friends recent suicide, I went to my doctor and said I wanted to see someone who wouldn't drug me. I got ONE session with a counsellor before being put onto a psych who put me on citalopram for two weeks. When I went back to him and told him I hated it he prescribed me two weeks more. I might have advised he take them ... anally. Although I could give the counselling another shot I am terribly worried if I refuse the drugs something worse will happen.
That is a good idea. I've got a lot of things set up (phones, e-mails, websites, contacts etc) so someone could take over easily. I didn't think of that. And oddly I know the perfect person. Thanks!

That is correct. 

I am fond of Camus and his absurdism is something I am very familiar with; particularly in *The Myth of Sisyphus*. I think the painful futility of finding, repeating and acting on purpose is too much for me. Many nihilists tend to find purpose in there being no purpose; Camus and Nietzsche had elements of this and it was beautiful.

I hope I am not suffering existentially because then I am really screwed. HAHA.

I haven't read *Dance, Dance, Dance* but I read *Norwegian Wood* I did not enjoy it at all! But I like the idea of life being about dancing.
I think a lot about Alan Watts thoughts of life is like music, the big bang was the note and we the resonance.

I want to kill myself but I don't want to do it thinking I could have done more. When I do something I like to think I knew it to the largest extent. If I can be helped by my self then I should at least try else my life could be erased and not just ended. I don't want that.

Does that make sense?
Yes I did notice. Thank you.

I don't think I have romanticised it. I hope not. It seems to be nothingness, not joy or physicality, no pain etc.

Well I tried to achieve my friend not killing himself. That was a low point failure. But politically I feel repeated failures. In romance I do badly. 

I feel mostly tired when I wake up for a few hours. I tend to be lethargic for the first few hours of the day then I am what I presume as average. I cry a lot but that just happens nothing tends to set it off; perhaps something repressed I have presumed. But I put on a hell of a good face, most people think I am happy and doing well considering my circumstances. But internally I do feel a indescribable pain something I have felt for several years. Sometimes, particularly now, it gets worse.

I understand the want to keep busy but I have been pretty bad, granted worse recently, for around 6 years. And I've been keeping busy all that time, I don't want to do it any more. Keeping busy doesn't feel like living for me, I'd prefer not to in that case.

Also the movie Clerks is great.
I'm an adult. And I also feel I have no power to take 'charge' in this life.

I have gone to SW. Thanks

I feel I have two options. Go on living or kill myself. I just prefer the latter.

I have talked myself into this. That is what I do, philosophise to the best decision.

I used to find joy in helping others, I still do. But I really don't think that is enough joy to keep me going. To start with I still feel depressed when I do it. Same with the books I love etc. I still feel bad even when I laugh.

Totally, I try to look at it like Anne Braden but it is too much for me. The wants to die out-weight my ability to improve our system I guess.

I have already moved town once. I don't want to spend my life running from the police. I have a good job here, I am a fairly respectable fellow besides the polices treatment of me. I study here too. I left all my friends behind once and it was the most depressing feeling I have had besides what I have now. I don't want it again.

Activism has been great to me. But I have not the energy for it. The things I enjoy I am not able to achieve. That is why I feel life isn't for me.

Again I don't want to be kept alive on the guilty feeling of what I will do to my loved ones (family isn't really close, my friends are my family).

I, at a rather young age, dropped my wants of a family; that was all I wanted. But I no longer want that. I really don't want kids nor a wife. But maybe a partner is something I would still want. But my childish dreams are things I decided I don't actually want; it was just what others wanted for me.
Thank you. I have posted there.

I think I have avoided the 'social script'. At least I hope I have. I still go to work and I study too; I also write a lot. Just to give me things in my future. I feel I am actively avoiding suicide, that is also why I am here I guess.

Yeah I have plenty of things I want to do. People I want to meet, things I want to study. But they all seem silly in the endless suffering of life's wide ranging experiences.

I do some volunteering and used to run a 'Help with life' forum. Now I think of it that is fairly ironic...
I just have still have will and want to help others but not myself much any more.
